logp.method_description: The ‘shake-flask’ method was used to determine the log Po/w value of natAuPNMP. This method requires the use of water-saturated octanol and octanol-saturated water, preventing artificial carry over between the two phases.13, 17 The solvents were prepared by shaking high grade octanol with ultra-pure water (resistivity = 18 MΩ cm-1). The two phases were allowed to equilibrate over 24 h before centrifugation and collection of the two saturated phases. The extinction coefficient of natAuPNMP was determined from a Beer–Lambert plot in octanol-saturated water and water-saturated octanol. It was necessary to determine the extinction coefficient in both solvent systems as the wavelength of maximum absorption (λmax) differed by 4 nm in the two solvent systems, and there was approximately 10% difference in extinction coefficient in each of the solvent systems. An aqueous solution of approximately 5 × 10-3 M concentration was prepared. This solution was shaken with an equal volume of water-saturated octanol and allowed to separate for 2 h before the solution was centrifuged to fully separate the two phases. The absorbance and hence concentrations of the chelate in each phase was determined by UV-visible spectroscopy. The experiment was performed in duplicate
